niche_preference_profile: This user most often prefers interfaces with strong visual hierarchy, clear action emphasis, rounded components, and relatively clean layouts. They repeatedly favor dark navy or dark high-contrast themes when paired with clear separation and vivid accents, but also show some support for light minimal layouts when those are cleaner and easier to scan. They prefer obvious buttons over text links, stronger selected/active states, grouped card-based structure, concise content presentation, and reduced clutter. They also consistently like softer rounded corners, pill buttons, and layouts that make the primary task or workspace visually dominant.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers strong hierarchy with prominent titles, clearly emphasized primary actions, obvious selected states, and layouts that guide attention in a clear top-down order.
Prefers cleaner, more minimal compositions with fewer competing elements, less decorative noise, and stronger focus on the main task or content area.
Prefers softer rounded corners across cards, inputs, panels, and especially pill-shaped buttons and chips.
Prefers content organized into distinct cards, grouped sections, or clearly separated modules rather than flatter undifferentiated layouts.
Prefers stronger contrast between surfaces, clearer borders or outlines, more defined containers, and more visible active or highlighted states.
Prefers concise copy, simplified details, and information arranged for quick scanning; often favors compact efficiency, though sometimes accepts more open spacing when it improves clarity.
Often prefers dark navy or dark high-contrast palettes with vivid cool or purple accents, especially when they create a polished, app-like, dashboard-style feel.
